items.title: Realising a prescribed finite residue field extension by a finite free ring map
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.source_version: Stacks Project git a04446e57ec1 (2026-07-28); file algebra.tex; corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma states that for a prime p of a ring R and a finite field extension L of the residue field at p, there is a finite free ring map R to S such that pS is prime with residue field extension isomorphic to the prescribed one (statement lines 44891-44899). The proof does not appeal to a structure theorem for finite free extensions: it inducts on the degree, reduces to an extension generated by one element, writes the coefficients of its minimal polynomial as images of elements of R after clearing a denominator outside p, absorbs that denominator by rescaling the generator, and then adjoins a root of the resulting monic polynomial (proof lines 44901-44918). The clearing and the rescaling of the generator are the steps that make the construction work. H2.
